en: Itivuttaka 38 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. This discourse was spoken by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Having said this, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One in the evening, having risen from his meditation, and after approaching and paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down at one side. As he was sitting there, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying, ‘Monks, these two things are to be cultivated by a bhikkhu who desires to attain the unshakable; what two?’—it would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would explain the meaning of this statement. “Then listen, Ānanda, and pay close attention; I will speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Ānanda, when a bhikkhu is possessed of two qualities, he is capable of attaining the unshakable. What two? He is possessed of a mind that is well-developed through concentration, and he is possessed of wisdom that has seen the truth. When a bhikkhu is possessed of these two qualities, he is capable of attaining the unshakable. Therefore, Ānanda, you too should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall be possessed of a mind that is well-developed through concentration, and we shall be possessed of wisdom that has seen the truth. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, the venerable Ānanda rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. *** Itivuttaka 39 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. The Discourse on Applied Thought.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Monks, two types of applied thought frequently occur to a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One: [the thought of renunciation and the thought of non-ill will]."
There is the thought of security and the thought of seclusion.
Monks, the Tathāgata delights in non-affliction and rejoices in non-affliction.
Toward that Tathāgata, monks, who delights in non-affliction and rejoices in non-affliction, this very thought frequently occurs:
‘By this mode of conduct, I do not harm anything, whether frail or firm.
Monks, the Tathāgata delights in seclusion and rejoices in seclusion.
Toward that Tathāgata, who delights in seclusion and rejoices in seclusion, this very reflection frequently occurs:
‘Whatever is unwholesome has been abandoned.
Therefore, monks, you too should dwell delighting in non-affliction and taking pleasure in non-affliction.
For you, monks, dwelling thus delighting in non-affliction and taking pleasure in non-affliction, this very thought will frequently occur to you:
‘By this mode of conduct we do not harm anything, whether moving or stationary.
Monks, dwell delighting in seclusion and rejoicing in seclusion.
For you, monks, who dwell delighting in seclusion and rejoicing in seclusion, this very thought will frequently arise:
“What is unwholesome? What has not been abandoned? What are we abandoning?
This is what the Blessed One said.
With reference to this, it is said:
“Two kinds of thoughts approach the Tathāgata, the Buddha, the one who accomplishes what was previously unaccomplished:
the first thought proclaimed is that of security.”
Then seclusion was declared as the second.
To that great sage who dispels darkness, who has gone to the further shore,
who has attained what is to be attained, who is self-controlled and free from taints;
One who has transcended craving, liberated through the destruction of craving—
that sage indeed bears his final body;
I call him a conqueror of Māra, one who has gone beyond old age.
Just as one standing on the summit of a mountain might see the people all around,
even so does the wise one, consisting of the Dhamma, [behold].
Having ascended the palace, the All-Seeing One,
free from sorrow, gazes upon the people overwhelmed by grief,
who are overcome by birth and old age.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The first.
